Week-one item **C** of #221. **Depends on A.** Shares an abstraction with #72, which wants the same pattern in the corpus loop and the effect pump.

Rulings this implements: #221's breaker ruling and its quota-feedback ruling; ADR-0061 Decision 7.

## What the sweep already settled

LiteLLM was rejected as the breaker on measured grounds: a five-second default cooldown, a failure **ratio** over the current minute rather than consecutive-N, no quality trip, no supported surface (`_set_cooldown_deployments` is private, no HTTP route), and cooldown transitions that never reach OTel. Evidence: `docs/research/multi-provider-routing-substrates.md`.

The availability half is **free on the Codex lane** — that provider publishes quota state first-party with a reset time — so the build is smaller than originally scoped.

## Scope

**Breaker**, one per lane, states closed / open / half-open, state in a file the dispatcher reads **before** dispatch:

- *Availability trip*, auto-reset, not an incident (#72's rule): `quota_exhausted` opens the lane until the **known** window reset — 5-hour and weekly boundaries are computable, so no guessed backoff.
- *Quality trip*, escalates rather than auto-resetting: N consecutive gate failures on one profile. This is the only thing that catches a provider swapping the model behind a name with no announcement.
- Every transition emits an OTel event.

**Quota feed**, per provider:

| Lane | Source |
|---|---|
| Claude | Status line stdin — `rate_limits.five_hour.{used_percentage,resets_at}`, `rate_limits.seven_day.{…}`. Pro/Max only, after the first API response; each window independently optional. A script chains the existing status line and writes the values into the breaker's state |
| Codex | `account/rateLimits/read` → `usedPercent`, `windowDurationMins`, `resetsAt`, `rateLimitReachedType`, plus an `account/rateLimits/updated` notification |
| z.ai | No machine-readable state exists. **Estimate** from our own dispatch ledger against the documented 5 h / 7 d caps and the time-of-day multiplier, and always label it estimated |

**Delivery to the orchestrator**: one line per lane, folded into `just watch-report`, which CLAUDE.md already says to run at the top of any turn. A verdict — open, or closed until a time — **not** three percentages. Per #209: where a rule-table already decides, do not hand an agent numbers to reason about.

## Weaknesses to carry, not solve

- The status line lives in the human's global `~/.claude/settings.json`, which this repository cannot govern, enforce or test. Prefer a polled provider endpoint wherever one exists.
- Status lines run only in interactive sessions; a headless orchestrator loses the Claude feed.
- Degraded fallback if the tap is absent: the dispatch path still sees 429s and trips the breaker on them — late, but not blind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dispatch to an open lane proceeds; to a closed lane it refuses with `quota_exhausted` and the reset time
- [ ] The quality trip fires on N consecutive gate failures and escalates rather than auto-resetting
- [ ] Transitions appear in OTel
- [ ] `just watch-report` prints one verdict line per lane, and stays silent about lanes that are fine
- [ ] The abstraction is usable by #72's two consumers, or the reason it is not is stated
- [ ] `just check`, `just unit` green

Refs #221, #72, #209
